planting.note: Plant dormant bushes in fall in full sun; like other pink and red currants it performs best where summers stay cool, struggling in regions with high heat and humidity.

directions: Plant dormant bushes in fall in full sun; this cultivar performs best where summers stay cool, struggling in regions with high heat and humidity. Pink Champagne is a popular pink-fruited selection of red currant, producing long, well-filled strigs of translucent, pale rose-pink berries that are noticeably milder and sweeter than typical red currants, making them pleasant for fresh eating straight off the bush rather than only for cooking. The self-fertile bush is vigorous and reliably productive, ripening its blush clusters in midsummer alongside or slightly ahead of most red currant cultivars. Culture is identical to red currant: grow in cool, well-drained, moisture-retentive soil with a pH of 6.0-6.5, mulch to keep roots cool, and prune each late winter to retain 8-12 mixed-age canes, removing wood older than five years since fruit forms best on younger spurwood. Net ripening clusters against birds, which find the pale, glowing fruit just as attractive as red currants. Check state Ribes restrictions before ordering, since currants are regulated in some areas as alternate hosts for white pine blister rust.

common_name: Dog Ridge Grape Rootstock (Vigorous Pierce's Disease-Tolerant Texas Understock)

planting.note: Plant dormant rootstock cuttings or rooted liners in spring in well-drained, sandy soil in full sun, then field bench-graft or bud a desired bunch or muscadine grape variety onto the young rootstock; Dog Ridge was selected from wild Vitis champinii vines found near Dog Ridge, Texas, for its exceptional vigor and drought tolerance.

directions: Dog Ridge (sometimes written Dogridge) is a wild Vitis champinii selection first collected near Dog Ridge, Texas, prized as one of the most vigorous and deep-rooted grape rootstocks available, giving grafted vines excellent drought tolerance and the ability to thrive in poor, sandy, or infertile soils where own-rooted bunch grapes struggle. Like the related Tampa rootstock, it confers meaningful tolerance to Pierce's disease, the bacterial infection spread by glassy-winged sharpshooters and other leafhoppers, and it also carries useful resistance to root-knot nematodes and phylloxera. Florida, Texas, and Gulf South growers choose between Dog Ridge and Tampa largely based on vigor and soil-type compatibility, since Dog Ridge tends to be the more vigorous of the two and is often favored on the poorest, driest sites. Bench-graft or bud a named bunch grape or muscadine cultivar onto young Dog Ridge rootstock in late winter or spring; left ungrafted, the vine is extremely rampant and produces only small, seedy black fruit of little culinary interest, so it is grown almost exclusively as an understock rather than for its own fruit.
sources: University of Florida IFAS Extension — Grape Breeding and Rootstock Program

common_name: Delizz Strawberry (F1 Seed-Grown Everbearing Patio Strawberry)

planting.note: Start seed indoors 8-10 weeks before last frost; surface-sow the fine seed and keep consistently moist and warm, since Delizz is an F1 hybrid bred to be grown true from seed rather than propagated from runners or crowns like most garden strawberries.

directions: Delizz is an F1 hybrid strawberry bred specifically to be raised from seed and fruit reliably in its first year, unlike most garden strawberry cultivars, which are propagated vegetatively from runners or crowns to preserve hybrid vigor. Surface-sow the fine seed indoors 8-10 weeks before the last frost, keeping it warm and consistently moist until germination, then transplant seedlings into full sun after frost danger passes. Plants stay compact and mounding, making Delizz a popular choice for hanging baskets, window boxes, and patio containers as well as small beds. It is day-neutral and everbearing, producing a steady succession of small to medium, sweet, aromatic red berries from summer through the first frosts rather than a single flush. Keep soil evenly moist while fruiting and deadhead spent trusses to encourage continued flowering; in cold climates it is commonly grown as an annual, though plants can overwinter with protection in milder zones.
